newsitem.title: CHINA: China Jan-May chemical exports up 23.6 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: China Jan-May chemical exports up 23.6 pct yr/yr.

text.p: China's exports of chemical products totalled $5.5 billion in the first five months of 1997, up 23.6 percent compared with the year-ago period, the Shenzhen-based Securities Times said on Monday.
But the domestic chemical industry has experienced sluggish sales, rising stockpiles and falling prices since the start of the year, the newspaper said.

Pre-tax profits of chemical firms covered in the state budget declined 25.9 percent year-on-year in the first half of 1997, with 48 percent of the firms registering losses in the first six months, it said.
Output of major chemical products -- including fertiliser and tyres -- showed steady growth during the first half, it said, but gave no further details.
The sales to production ratio of domestic chemical firms stood at 94.4 percent for the January-June period, down 0.4 percentage points year-on-year, the newspaper said.
